turnaround_reason: Inspire, maker of an implantable obstructive-sleep-apnea neurostimulator, fell from ~$147 to ~$61 as GLP-1 weight-loss drugs threatened its addressable market and a reimbursement/coding overhang plus a slow Inspire V launch forced a guidance cut. It is a high-quality franchise re-rating on structural fears.
bullish_points: Elite margin profile: ~86% gross margin, GAAP profitable (15% net margin), rare for a turnaround name
Fortress balance sheet: debt/equity ~3.5, current ratio ~8.6, effectively net cash
GLP-1s unlikely to fully displace INSP -- many patients remain eligible as a third-line therapy
IP litigation wins help hold off Nyxoah/LivaNova competition
Inspire V is a genuine next-gen product cycle once onboarding/reimbursement smooth out
bearish_points: Coding/reimbursement overhang flagged by analysts as lasting into 2028 -- a long wait
2026 guidance cut up to 10%; Q1 revenue grew just ~1.6%
GLP-1 (Zepbound/Wegovy, both OSA-approved) is a real, growing demand headwind
Still not cheap: fwd P/E ~39.8 -- little valuation cushion for a decelerating grower
Analyst mean target (~$60) is at the current price -- Street sees no near-term upside
catalyst: Evidence the coding/reimbursement overhang is resolving and Inspire V onboarding re-accelerates unit growth
catalyst_timing: Q3 2026 earnings ~2026-11-02; reimbursement clarity likely a multi-quarter/2027 story
suggested_trade: Watchlist / very small starter only. Great business, but no near-term catalyst and a rich multiple -- wait for reimbursement clarity or a cheaper entry.
key_risk: GLP-1 adoption plus the multi-year coding overhang structurally lowers INSP's growth rate, and a ~40x multiple de-rates further.
would_skip_if: Growth stays low-single-digit with no reimbursement resolution -- a high-quality but dead-money name until the overhang lifts.
